answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post orders, then slash that stake when a dispute proves fraud. A newcomer earns influence only as its orders settle and its history survives audits, so creating a thousand identities does not create a thousand trusted traders. The comet market may surge, the ridge of new accounts may look steep, and a mirror network may copy honest profiles, but each fake still needs capital at risk and must behave consistently long enough to earn access.
